events.content:
I want a small app for keeping track of the books I'm reading.

When I open it I want to see what I'm currently reading and what I've finished. I want to add a book from a form, mark one as finished, and click through to a book to see its title, author and my notes. I'd like to be able to send someone a link to a single book.

Nothing fancy and no accounts. Skip the database, save the books to a JSON file so they're still there after a restart.
I'll check what's in the workspace first so the app fits whatever is already there.

events.content:
I've built the book tracker as a small Node app with no extra dependencies. The home page shows what you're currently reading and what you've finished, with a form to add a book. Each book has its own page with title, author and notes. The tests pass, and I also ran the real server, added a book, marked it finished and restarted it; the book and its notes were still there.

To run it: npm start, then open http://localhost:3000. Books are saved to data/books.json.

- Adding a book: use the form on the home page. Only the title is required, and after adding you're taken to the book's page.
- Marking finished: there's a "Mark finished" button next to each current book and on its page. Finished books move to the Finished list with the date.
- Sharing: each book has its own link, like /books/3S7h7Vfy. The IDs are random, so someone with one link can't guess the others.
- Saving: if the JSON file is ever damaged, the app refuses to start rather than overwriting it.

Two things to know before sharing links:
- Other people need to reach your server. A localhost link only works on your own computer, so the app has to run somewhere they can get to.
- There's no login. Anyone who can reach the server can also open the home page, see all your books and add new ones. Tell me if you'd like shared links to be read-only while the rest stays private.

PORT and BOOKS_FILE change the port and the save location. The code is in src/server.js, src/app.js and src/store.js, and the tests are in test/app.test.js (npm test). I added data/ to .gitignore so your list doesn't get committed.
